# AutoSugges autocomplete

AutoSugges is a hosted, edge-served autocomplete and list-of-values service. A published list (countries, NAICS, airports, currencies, cities...) is queried with a publishable key, and the answer is a short ranked list of suggestions. Site: https://autosugges.com. Docs: https://docs.autosugges.com.

## Rules
- Only autocomplete queries. Call `GET /v1/query` with the text the user typed. Never fetch, dump, export or download a whole list, and never enumerate one with sequential queries.
- The publishable key goes in the `key` query parameter. Never send it in an `Authorization` header; that header is reserved for an optional access token on a protected list.
- Minimum query length is 2 characters and is never 1. Send no request below the list's `queryPolicy.minQueryChars`.
- Debounce 150 ms by default. Read the real value from `queryPolicy.debounceMs`; do not hardcode either number.
- A list returns 10 suggestions by default. Render what is returned; do not page or request more.
- Render `displayValue`, store `value`. Switch on the typed error `code`, never on a message string.
- A failure is not "no results". Show an error state driven by the error code.

## Request contract
- `GET https://runtime.autosugges.com/v1/bootstrap?key=<publishable key>` — Resolves the list identity, the active version hash and the effective query policy for this key. Call once per session before querying. Key placement: `key` query parameter.
- `GET https://runtime.autosugges.com/v1/query?key=<publishable key>&q=<text>&locale=<optional BCP-47 tag>` — Returns the pre-ranked suggestions for one query. Key placement: `key` query parameter.
- Optional `POST /v1/selection` reports which suggestion was chosen. Skipping it costs ranking quality only.
- `queryPolicy.minQueryChars` — Minimum characters before a query is legal. Never below 2, and never hardcoded — a shorter query is rejected and not billed.
- `queryPolicy.debounceMs` — How long to wait after the last keystroke before issuing a query.

## Frameworks

### React

Mount the shipped accessible combobox in a React component — debounce, cancellation, keyboard navigation and ARIA are already wired.

Install: `npm install @autosugges/client`

- React integration guide: https://docs.autosugges.com/integrations/react

### Next.js

Keep the input in a Client Component and the page around it a Server Component, so only the interactive part ships JavaScript.

Install: `npm install @autosugges/client`

- Next.js integration guide: https://docs.autosugges.com/integrations/nextjs

### JavaScript (no framework)

Mount an accessible autocomplete on an ordinary HTML page from a data attribute, with no framework and no hand-written combobox markup.

Install: No install step. Load the prebuilt browser build with a <script> tag: <script src="https://autosugges.com/sdk/v1/autosugges.js"></script>, or from the jsDelivr CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@autosugges/client/dist/browser/autosugges.js. For a pinned build use the immutable `/sdk/v1/autosugges.<hash>.js`; `/sdk/v1/autosugges.js` always resolves to the current v1 build.

- JavaScript integration guide: https://docs.autosugges.com/integrations/vanilla-js

### Expo / React Native

Compose the autocomplete from React Native primitives, with the accessibility semantics supplied by the SDK’s native binding.

Install: `npm install @autosugges/client`

- Expo integration guide: https://docs.autosugges.com/integrations/expo

## Security
- A publishable key is public by design. It is safe in client-side JavaScript, in a mobile bundle, and in a page a search engine can read. It is not a secret and does not need a proxy.
- A publishable key is not a substitute for origin control: keys are bound to an allow-list of origins, and a request from an origin the tenant has not allowed is refused with `origin_not_allowed` and is not billed. Add the deploying site’s origin in the AutoSugges dashboard before going live.
- Never place a secret key, a signing key, a service-role credential or a database URL in client code, in an environment variable prefixed for browser exposure, or in a prompt. Nothing in an AutoSugges browser or mobile integration needs one.
- An access token (`authorization: Bearer …`) is only for a list whose policy requires one. It is short-lived, and it is minted by your own server from your own AutoSugges credentials — never in the browser, never hardcoded, never committed.
- Do not log the raw query text or the response body. Log the typed error `code` and the `requestId`.

## Errors
Every failure carries a typed `code`. Switch on it; retry only the retryable ones, with backoff.

- Retryable: `rate_limited`, `compile_failed`, `artifact_unavailable`, `internal_error`.
- Not retryable: `invalid_key`, `origin_not_allowed`, `invalid_list`, `subscription_required`, `list_not_published`, `token_expired`, `invalid_token`, `quota_exceeded`, `query_too_short`, `query_too_long`, `invalid_request`, `challenge_failed`, `publish_validation_failed`, `resource_removed`, `invalid_domain`, `domain_validation_failed`, `forbidden`.
- Remediation for each code: https://docs.autosugges.com/api-reference/errors

## MCP server

```sh
claude mcp add autosugges -e AUTOSUGGES_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=pk_live_... -- npx -y @autosugges/mcp
```

Other MCP clients: command `npx`, args `-y @autosugges/mcp`, env `AUTOSUGGES_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`. Tools: `search_list` (bounded), `list_datasets`, `get_dataset` (metadata only), `get_integration_instructions`. Free key: https://app.autosugges.com.
